reconciliation.prior_vs_new: The earlier absence statement and the new existence measurement are different-provenance observations at different times. The earlier operator-reported state is not restated as a host measurement; the new host-captured state supersedes it as current reported state. No contradiction in authority: DISP-01 is a rule about which ancestor to evaluate, not a claim that the parent must be absent.
reconciliation.no_allegation: No allegation of unauthorized creation; the mere existence of the directories, with unknown provenance, is not a finding that any preflight, operator workaround, or unauthorized act created them.
reconciliation.no_causal_claim: No inference from the 2026-10-26 creation dates, from the earlier REV2 capture, from the corrected traversal, or from the instrument digest about who or what created the directories. P-1 remains unexecuted.
reconciliation.materiality: Under the exact effective criteria (successor act §8 step 1; PF-11/PF-12 and PF-13 as read by DISP-01; PF-15 act §4), creation provenance is NOT a criterion. The criteria test current absolute/local-fixed-NTFS/outside-worktree/non-synchronized/non-elevated-writable characteristics and store + sidecar absence. Provenance is material only to the PF-12/DISP-01 prohibition on the preflight itself creating store-path directories; no supplied evidence shows the preflight created them, and the store/sidecars remain absent.
reconciliation.provenance_disposition: RECORDED AS UNKNOWN — neither converted into a pass nor into an assumed failure; not a new authority blocker.

disp_01_application.pre_creating_clause_reading: DISP-01 says pre-creating the terminal parent outside the authorized execution remains unauthorized and a STOP. That clause governs a deliberate preflight/workaround action to satisfy PF-13; it is not a rule that a directory whose provenance is unknown becomes a STOP merely because it exists. It would be engaged only by evidence that the preflight or an operator workaround created it. No such evidence is supplied.
